headline: Planning is imagining future states and working backward—a distinctly human ability to shape tomorrow from today
universal_truth: The future rewards those who prepare for it; today's actions create tomorrow's options
fun_facts: The ability to plan ahead may be unique to humans—most animals live in the present
Writing down plans makes them 42% more likely to be achieved, according to some studies
The best plans include contingencies—what to do when things don't go as expected
discussion_questions: How far ahead do you typically plan?
What happens when you don't plan?
How do you balance planning with flexibility?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Only humans can vividly imagine next year and take action today because of it. We can simulate futures that don't exist, choose one we prefer, and work backward to make it happen. Planning is mental time travel that shapes reality.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Planning seems obviously useful, yet many people avoid it. They live reactively, responding to whatever happens. Why is planning hard, and why is it worth the effort?

options.text: Planning converts vague intentions into specific actions and reveals obstacles before you hit them—it increases odds of reaching goals
options.response: Yes. Plans turn wishes into roadmaps. The act of planning surfaces problems, sequences steps, and creates commitment. Without plans, intentions stay dreams.

options.text: Plans reduce anxiety by giving you a sense of control
options.response: Anxiety reduction is one benefit, but the practical value of planning comes from improved outcomes...

q1.title: Mental Simulation
q1.script: Planning is running simulations. You imagine taking actions and predict their consequences. This mental rehearsal reveals obstacles before they appear and lets you prepare responses. Planning is cheap failure—learning without paying the full price.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Mental Simulation"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Working Backward
q2.script: Effective planning often works backward from the goal. What needs to be true right before success? What enables that? Keep stepping back until you reach today. This reveals the critical path and necessary milestones.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Plans vs Planning
q3.script: Eisenhower said 'plans are useless, but planning is indispensable.' The plan itself will change. But the process of planning builds understanding, reveals dependencies, and prepares your mind. The thinking matters more than the document.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: The future rewards those who prepare for it. Planning teaches that today's actions create tomorrow's options. Think ahead—even if the plan changes, the thinking won't be wasted.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 185. Tomorrow, we'll explore putting things in order—organization. Until then, choose one goal and work backward: what needs to happen first?
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Backward Planning - Map a Goal
growTrack.activity: Choose something you want to accomplish. Work backward: what's the step right before success? What enables that step? Keep going until you reach an action you can take today. This is how distant goals become immediate actions.
